articles.title: 比亚迪悬赏 50 万至 500 万元征集 MCN 黑公关线索，已有多人被拘
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，比亚迪法务部刚刚发布公告，集中披露了近期多起网络侵权案件的处理进展。公告显示，已有人员因编造、散布涉比亚迪不实信息被公安机关处以拘留处罚，多个网络账号经法院审理被判构成侵权。在已披露的案件中，冯某、季某因恶意编造涉比亚迪不实信息并在社交平台散布，比亚迪报警后，公安机关认定二人行为扰乱公共秩序，已依法予以拘留。另一案件中，姜某在抖音平台长期、多次发布侮辱及诋毁比亚迪的言论，同样被公安机关认定违法并处以拘留。针对网络账号“娱乐”“车界”“四五”“司机”等长期发布诋毁性言论的行为，比亚迪提起诉讼后，法院认定构成侵权，判令相关主体公开道歉并赔偿经济损失。比亚迪还专门提及 MCN 机构的有组织行为。据介绍，部分 MCN 机构旗下账号集中发布针对比亚迪的文章，涉及机构包括“涅”“远”“马”“牛”“洲”等数十家，其中一些账号借助 AI 生成标题雷同、行文相似的同质化内容，并以“辟谣式传谣”方式发布。比亚迪表示已完成证据保全，正采取法律手段追责。悬赏机制方面，比亚迪此次针对 MCN 等有组织抹黑行为的线索，将奖励区间设为 50 万元至 500 万元；其他符合条件的线索提供者，奖励区间为 5 万元至 500 万元。线索提交渠道为 @比亚迪新闻打假办公室及邮箱 xwdj.office@byd.com。IT之家注：比亚迪的举报悬赏机制始于 2021 年 12 月，最初奖励上限为 100 万元，2022 年 6 月将上限提升至 500 万元并延续至今。比亚迪在公告中同时表示，尊重并接受社会各界的建议和监督，但将对侮辱、造谣、抹黑等侵权行为持续以法律手段维权。

articles.title: 黄仁勋卸任英伟达 CEO：约 1.08 亿美元股权奖励作废，约占其身价的 0.08%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，彭博社昨日（11 月 12 日）发布博文，英伟达联合创始人、前首席执行官黄仁勋在被董事会罢免后，将失去约 1.08 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 7.22 亿元人民币）的未归属股权激励。这一金额虽然庞大，但仅相当于其约 1,384 亿美元（现汇率约合 9,252.14 亿元人民币）净资产的 0.08%。根据英伟达的股权激励政策，高管一旦终止连续任职，其尚未归属的限制性股票单位（RSU）将被没收。黄仁勋目前持有约 34.6 万份此类单位；若公司业绩达标，他原本还可通过股权激励计划获得约 31 万股股票。与许多依赖期权或长期激励的科技企业掌门人不同，黄仁勋的财富主要来自其直接持有的英伟达普通股。彭博亿万富翁指数显示，他持有公司约 3.5% 的投票权，这部分持股约占其总财富的近 97%。由于英伟达只有一类股份，他并不享有特殊投票权。黄仁勋的离职直接冲击了英伟达股价。消息公布后，公司股价在纽约一度重挫 14%，随后跌幅收窄，最终收跌 4.3%，报 166.19 美元（现汇率约合 1,111 元人民币）；仅此一个交易日，黄仁勋的个人净资产便蒸发超过 60 亿美元（现汇率约合 401.1 亿元人民币）。

articles.title: 马斯克谈黄仁勋结束 33 年掌舵英伟达生涯：创始人很难被取代
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，英伟达创始人黄仁勋昨日（11 月 12 日）宣布辞去公司总裁、首席执行官及董事职务，即刻生效，结束其长达 33 年的掌舵生涯。对此全球首富埃隆 · 马斯克（Elon Musk）认为，创始人很难被取代。硅谷知名投资人纳瓦尔 · 拉维坎特（Naval Ravikant）发推文称，从苹果联合创始人史蒂夫 · 乔布斯（Steve Jobs）和优步联合创始人特拉维斯 · 卡兰尼克（Travis Kalanick）的经历看，创始人并非“随随便便就能被取代”。马斯克回应“True words”，即“说得没错”，公开表达认同。IT之家注：乔布斯于 1985 年因与苹果管理层及董事会的权力斗争离开苹果。此后苹果产品线混乱、市场份额下滑，到 1990 年代中期一度濒临财务危机。苹果于 1997 年收购乔布斯创办的 NeXT，他重返公司并主导 iMac、iPod、iPhone 等产品周期，带领苹果完成商业史上罕见的复兴。卡兰尼克是 Uber 联合创始人，2017 年在性骚扰指控、管理文化争议和投资者压力下辞去 CEO 职务。Uber 随后由达拉 · 科斯罗萨西接任，公司逐步改善治理、稳定运营，并实现持续盈利。创始人一旦离开，公司能否顺利延续其愿景、文化和执行力，并不确定，创始人本身也不容易由外部职业经理人简单替代。

articles.title: TCL 华星 CEO 赵军：印刷 OLED 已实现量产出货，广州 t8 项目计划明年 5 月产品点亮
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，在今日的 TCL 华星全球显示生态大会 DTC 2026 上，TCL 华星 CEO 赵军宣布，经过 13 年的研发，搭载印刷 OLED 屏幕的电竞产品今年已实现量产出货，从专业显示走向主流消费市场。而这仅仅是开始，TCL 华星广州 t8 主厂房已经提前封顶，计划于明年 5 月份产品点亮，明年第四季度实现量产。据官方介绍，作为 TCL 华星面向下一代显示技术布局的战略性项目，t8 项目是印刷 OLED 技术实现产业升级的重要载体。项目总投资约 295 亿元，设计月加工玻璃基板能力约 2.25 万片，主要产品涵盖平板、笔记本电脑、显示器等应用领域，可延伸至柔性、折叠显示屏。IT之家注意到，该项目自 2025 年 9 月 16 日正式打桩以来，历时 226 天完成主厂房封顶，刷新了行业最快封顶纪录。TCL 华星方面称，印刷 OLED 采用喷墨打印工艺，将有机发光材料以“按需沉积”方式精准印刷到玻璃基板上，相比传统真空蒸镀，具备材料利用率更高、生产更绿色高效等显著优势，是业界公认的下一代显示技术的重要路线。联想今年初在 CES 2026 展示了一款卷轴屏笔记本，搭载的就是 TCL 华星印刷 OLED 屏幕。

articles.title: 22.5~26 万元比亚迪第三代唐预售：定位大五座旗舰 SUV 车型，续航 770~850km
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，比亚迪第三代唐今日正式开启预售，预售价区间为 22.5 万元至 26 万元，IT之家汇总如下：850km 后驱激光尊荣型 22.5 万元850km 后驱激光旗舰型 24 万元770km 四驱型 26 万元路天表示，全国比亚迪王朝 4S 店已陆续到车，欢迎大家到店体验第三代唐，先体验再下订。第三代唐在外观上提供 3 款双拼色与 5 款单色共 8 种车色。车头搭载 2.5 米一体贯穿式飞檐光羽大灯，车尾则采用凤翎中国结尾灯与凤凰展翅迎宾光毯。车身长度超过 5 米，轴距接近 3 米，全系采用五座布局，二排腿部空间达到 1003mm，靠背最大仰角为 130 度。座舱是第三代唐此次变化最集中的区域。车内提供三幅式双拼色圆形方向盘与椭圆形单色方向盘两种选择，座椅以 Nappa 真皮包覆，全车四座均配备通风、加热及 10 点独立按摩。副驾为零重力座椅，二排座椅支持超过 12 种常用变化形态。智能化配置的核心是一组双屏布局：35.4 英寸一体远端星环屏负责呈现车速、导航等行车信息，30 英寸全景巨幕屏承担交互与娱乐功能。车机首发 AI 萌宠桌面与时光壁纸，语音助手“迪迪虾”支持方言识别与模糊指令，并具备全舱声纹识别能力。储物方面，第三代唐设有 205L 电动开闭前备箱（带排水孔）、910L 后备箱（二排放倒后可拓展至 2098L），以及 6.8L 车载冷暖冰箱，全车提供超过 28 处扩展接口与磁吸点。三电系统上，第三代唐搭载第二代刀片电池与闪充技术，CLTC 纯电续航最高 850km（对应后驱版），四驱版续航为 770km。后驱版电机功率 300kW，四驱版系统综合功率 515kW，零百加速 4.3 秒，该数据对应四驱双电机版本。IT之家注：CLTC 为中国轻型汽车行驶工况，是国内纯电动车续航标注的测试标准。底盘采用前双叉臂、后五连杆独立悬架结构，官方信息显示搭载云辇-A 双腔空气悬架。不过，部分渠道流传的配置描述称入门版本可能配备云辇-C，空气悬架仅提供给高配车型，截至预售启动时官方尚未公布完整配置表，最终规格以正式上市时发布的配置信息为准。安全方面，第三代唐采用 13 横 9 纵笼式车身，全系标配 11 个安全气囊，并搭载天神之眼 B 辅助驾驶激光版，支持城市领航与智能泊车辅助，同时配备 TBC 高速爆胎稳行系统。

articles.title: OpenAI 最新一轮私募融资 150 亿美元，融前估值 1.25 万亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，据 CNBC 今日报道，OpenAI 在最新一轮私募融资中筹集了 150 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,002.76 亿元人民币），公司融资前估值达到 1.25 万亿美元（现汇率约合 8.36 万亿元人民币）。这一金额高于此前媒体披露的约 110 亿美元，此次融资也被视为 OpenAI 为 2027 年潜在首次公开募股（IPO）提前准备资金的重要举措。知情人士对 CNBC 表示，此次融资尚未正式结束，预计将在未来几周内完成。相关人士将其描述为一次机会性融资，旨在帮助 OpenAI 为预计于 2027 年进行的 IPO 做准备。与此同时，其主要竞争对手 Anthropic 正在筹备纳斯达克上市，计划于 11 月 19 日开始交易。根据路透社此前报道，Anthropic 此次 IPO 的估值目标最高约为 1.4 万亿美元（现汇率约合 9.36 万亿元人民币）。融资规模扩大之际，OpenAI 的营收增长与巨额运营亏损也成为投资者关注的焦点。据《华尔街日报》披露的数据，OpenAI 2026 年第三季度营收约为 100 亿美元，较第二季度增长近 50%。不过，公司同期运营亏损达到 109 亿美元，高于第二季度的 101 亿美元。其调整后营业利润率则从第二季度的约 -150% 改善至 -109%。这些数据反映出 OpenAI 在扩大业务规模的同时，仍需承担模型训练、推理服务以及数据中心等基础设施建设带来的高额成本。尽管营收持续增长，但公司距离实现持续盈利仍有较大距离。相比之下，Anthropic 的财务表现也受到市场关注。不过，不同人工智能企业对股权激励、慈善捐款等项目的财务调整方式并不完全相同，因此直接比较两家公司的调整后利润率需要谨慎。随着 Anthropic 即将登陆公开市场，以及 OpenAI 将潜在 IPO 时间指向 2027 年，投资者有望通过上市公司的财务披露，更直接地比较两家企业的营收增长、运营成本和盈利能力。相关阅读：《消息称 OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元首期新融资，估值 1.25 万亿美元》

articles.title: 黄仁勋辞职后，英伟达总部外出现鲜花和蜡烛
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，科技媒体 Business Insider 昨日（11 月 12 日）发布博文，报道称在美国加州圣克拉拉的英伟达总部外，有人于公司标志前摆放多束鲜花，并放置了一支装在玻璃罐中的白色蜡烛，被外界视为致敬黄仁勋这位 AI 时代标志性人物。现场画面显示，一名路人将玻璃罐装蜡烛放在“NVIDIA”标志前；鲜花则整齐靠在标志下方。这些物品没有附带留言，但被外界视为告别与致敬刚刚辞去首席执行官职务的联合创始人黄仁勋。IT之家附上相关推文截图如下：黄仁勋执掌英伟达长达 33 年，是公司从图形芯片厂商成长为全球 AI 算力核心供应商的关键人物。他的突然离任，令不少员工感到震动与失落；有报道称，部分员工在消息公布后落泪，内部也弥漫着对公司未来走向的焦虑。据职场匿名平台 Blind 于 11 月 9 日至 10 日对 232 名英伟达员工进行的调查，88% 的受访者希望黄仁勋继续留任；11% 认为他应主动辞职，仅 1% 支持董事会将其免职。值得注意的是，该员工调查的样本规模仅为 232 人，且投票时间早于辞职相关报道，因此不能代表英伟达全体员工的真实意见。与英伟达员工形成对比的是，Blind 另一项针对 1,689 名各行业专业人士的调查显示，60% 支持黄仁勋留任，18% 认为他应主动辞职，22% 希望董事会将其撤换。

articles.title: 中芯国际赵海军：中国客户需求增速高于公司整体需求增速
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，据财联社报道，中芯国际联合 CEO 赵海军 13 日在三季度业绩会上表示，三季度销售收入以地区分类看，中国、美国占比分别为 90.8%、7.8%；从金额来看，中国销售收入环比增长 7%，主要原因为中国客户需求增长速度高于公司整体需求增长速度，公司相应调配产能，满足客户需求。晶圆收入按尺寸分，十二英寸和八英寸占比平稳，分别为 79% 和 21%；从金额来看，12 英寸和 8 英寸晶圆收入环比分别增长 9% 和 4%，主要原因为客户需求饱满，且公司扩产以 12 英寸产线为主。展望未来，赵海军认为行业确定性主要体现在两方面：一是人工智能需求有望拉长半导体上行周期，增长结构与周期形态随之变化；二是全产业链在地化大发展仍在延续。在此背景下，公司依托与客户的战略绑定，配合中国客户创新速度，将特色和客制化工艺优势做强。基于此，公司以客户需求为导向推进产能扩充，以高附加值优质产品组合构筑领先优势，努力稳定 EBITDA—— 也就是经营现金流能力，提升成本管控与运营效率，增强穿越周期的经营韧性，实现有质量、可持续的增长。IT之家注意到，中芯国际 11 月 12 日发布 2026 年前三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）及第三季度（2026 年 7 月～2026 年 9 月）报告：2026 年前三季度营业总收入：606.18 亿元，同比增长 22.4%归母净利润：73.14 亿元，同比增长 91.6%经营现金流：286.25 亿元基本每股收益：0.91 元稀释每股收益：0.91 元2026 年第三季度营业总收入：219.83 亿元，同比增长 28.1%归母净利润：28.47 亿元，同比增长 87.6%经营现金流：78.66 亿元基本每股收益：0.33 元稀释每股收益：0.33 元

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，中芯国际联合 CEO 赵海军在三季度业绩会上表示，从晶圆收入的应用端来看，智能手机和消费电子需求仍较为疲弱，两者环比分别下降 8% 和 1%。赵海军指出，电脑与平板、工业与汽车、互联与可穿戴市场整体需求没有大的变化。但公司受益于产业链本土化切换和前瞻性平台部署，这三个领域的收入分别实现 26%、26% 和 18% 的环比增长。他还提到，公司业绩淡季不淡，虽然手机、部分消费类订单有所走弱，但公司充分发挥多工艺平台的协调性调配能力，将释放出来的产能向专用存储、BCD 等高需求、高附加值产品倾斜。四季度，公司预计出货量保持稳健，产品组合变化及价格随行就市推动平均销售单价上涨，预计收入环比增长 4% 到 6%；同时，折旧、原材料等成本压力持续增加，以及四季度公司增加工程和研发投片量，使得产能利用率在扩产产能持续释放的基础上略有下降，所以给出的毛利率指引与上季度指引持平，为 26% 到 28%。赵海军表示，公司全年销售收入预计超过 120 亿美元（现汇率约合 802.21 亿元人民币），较去年同期增长接近三成；在折旧总额较去年增长约三成的情况下，毛利率预计在 26% 左右，同比增加约 5 个百分点。同时全球设备供应链整体紧张，交付周期拉长，部分设备交付时间仍存在不确定性，虽不会影响今年的扩产规划落地，但可能对全年的资本开支执行带来扰动。展望未来，他认为行业确定性主要体现在两方面：一是人工智能需求有望拉长半导体上行周期，增长结构与周期形态随之变化；二是全产业链在地化大发展仍在延续。在此背景下，公司依托与客户的战略绑定，配合中国客户创新速度，将特色和客制化工艺优势做强。基于此，公司以客户需求为导向推进产能扩充，以高附加值优质产品组合构筑领先优势，努力稳定 EBITDA—— 也就是经营现金流能力，提升成本管控与运营效率，增强穿越周期的经营韧性，实现有质量、可持续的增长。中芯国际第三季度财报主要数据如下：2026 年前三季度营业总收入：606.18 亿元，同比增长 22.4%归母净利润：73.14 亿元，同比增长 91.6%经营现金流：286.25 亿元基本每股收益：0.91 元稀释每股收益：0.91 元2026 年第三季度营业总收入：219.83 亿元，同比增长 28.1%归母净利润：28.47 亿元，同比增长 87.6%经营现金流：78.66 亿元基本每股收益：0.33 元稀释每股收益：0.33 元在工业与汽车领域，中芯国际全面布局 BCD 低中高电压产品，提供多样化的特色器件与工艺，最高支持 grade 0 车规标准。IT之家注：grade 0 为汽车电子元器件温度等级中的最高档，要求工作温度范围覆盖-40℃ 至 150℃。产品覆盖 BMS 模拟前端与系统基础芯片、数字隔离、隔离驱动和采样前端以及智能功率开关，以满足相关客户的增量需求，特别是高附加值产品的需求。相关阅读：《中芯国际赵海军：第三季度平均晶圆单价环比提升 1.8%》《中芯国际联合 CEO 赵海军：预计 2026 年收入超过 120 亿美元，全球设备交付周期拉长》《中芯国际 2026 年前三季度归母净利润 73.14 亿元，同比增长 91.6%》

articles.title: 消息称英伟达前 CEO 黄仁勋同意在感恩节前赴国会作证，具体日期仍在协商
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，彭博社昨日报道，佛罗里达州共和党籍众议员、美国众议院外交事务委员会主席布莱恩 · 马斯特（Brian Mast）当地时间周四表示，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋已同意在感恩节（11 月 26 日星期四）前赴国会作证，但具体日期尚未确定。马斯特称：“他已经同意到场，我们正在协商具体日期。”IT之家附上相关截图如下：此次作证预计将涉及多个国会委员会，包括外交事务委员会、众议院情报委员会以及众议院特别委员会。马斯特表示，作证很可能在宣誓后进行，并会被记录、转录，甚至录像；目前尚不清楚听证会是否公开举行，但外界普遍预计可能采取闭门形式。马斯特强调，英伟达对美国而言“非常重要”，他不希望公司受到伤害，但黄仁勋需要回答“非常严肃的问题”。分析人士认为，此次国会作证将成为观察美国如何在国家安全、科技竞争与商业利益之间寻求平衡的重要窗口。

articles.title: 罕见双星系统被发现：每隔约 8 分钟向地球方向发出规律无线电脉冲
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，澳大利亚科廷大学及国际射电天文学研究中心（ICRAR）的研究团队宣布，发现一个距地球超过 5,000 光年的罕见双星系统，编号为 GPM J071507−114,153。该系统由一颗白矮星和一颗类似太阳的 G 型恒星组成，白矮星每约 7.9 分钟自转一周，并向地球方向发出规律的无线电脉冲。相关研究已发表于《自然 · 天文学》。白矮星是恒星耗尽燃料后留下的致密核心，体积小、密度极高。研究团队首先利用澳大利亚的默奇森宽视场阵列（MWA）在银河系巡天中发现该信号，随后借助南非 MeerKAT 射电望远镜定位，并通过夏威夷凯克天文台的光学观测确认其伴星是一颗 G 型恒星。该发现是科学家首次在“白矮星＋类太阳恒星”的双星组合中探测到周期性无线电脉冲。此前已知类似系统多由白矮星与较小、较冷的红矮星构成；新结果说明，产生这类“长周期暂现源”信号的恒星组合可能比既有认识更加多样。研究人员分析超过 100 小时的射电数据后，首次清晰观测到白矮星绕伴星运行的运动特征，从而判断无线电脉冲来自白矮星附近，甚至可能直接来自白矮星本身。团队推测，白矮星的强磁场可能加速来自伴星恒星风的带电粒子，当辐射束扫过地球时，便形成如同“宇宙灯塔”般的规律脉冲。该系统属于“长周期暂现源”（LPT）：这类天体以数分钟至数小时的间隔发射无线电信号，其物理机制尚未完全弄清。此次发现不仅确认了一个罕见的双星组合，也为破解银河系中神秘周期性射电信号的来源提供了关键线索。IT之家附上参考地址A long-period transient with a Sun-like companion

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 13 日消息，据新华社昨日报道，华中科技大学公共卫生学院院长潘安教授团队联合多国专家完成了一项研究，已于 11 月 12 日发表在《自然》上。该研究基于中国、英国、美国、西班牙四国四大队列、共计 84.4 万余名成年人的数据，系统验证了《柳叶刀-糖尿病与内分泌学》委员会 2025 年提出的精细化肥胖诊断框架。结论明确：仅凭 BMI 诊断肥胖，会造成相当比例的漏诊与误诊。BMI 长期被用作肥胖筛查的核心指标，但它只能反映体重与身高的比例关系，无法区分增加的体重来自脂肪还是肌肉，也无法判断脂肪是否已对器官功能造成损害。潘安在研究中指出，这一“天然缺陷”在临床中直接表现为两类错误：一部分体脂过多、已出现器官功能受损的人，因 BMI 未达到肥胖阈值而被漏诊；另一部分 BMI 超标但体脂并未过多的人，则被误判为肥胖。研究数据显示，与精细化框架相比，单纯依据 BMI 会使 5.2% 至 8.6% 的参与者肥胖程度被低估，同时使 1.2% 至 3.1% 的参与者被高估。论文共同作者、伦敦国王学院教授弗朗切斯科 · 鲁比诺表示，更准确地识别和定义肥胖病例，有助于改善患者结局。《柳叶刀》委员会提出的框架将体脂过多人群区分为“临床肥胖”与“临床前肥胖”。临床肥胖要求存在由肥胖导致的器官功能受损或日常活动受限；临床前肥胖则指体脂超标但器官功能尚未受损的状态。在体脂过多者中，仅 22.7% 至 31.3% 达到临床肥胖标准，其余大多数处于临床前阶段。两类状态对应的健康风险差异显著。在超过 10 年的追踪随访中，临床前肥胖者的全因死亡风险较健康人群增加 19%，而临床肥胖者的死亡风险则上升至 69%。研究同时发现，约 77% 至 91% 的临床前肥胖者并未在随访期内进展为临床肥胖，提示在器官功能尚未受损的阶段进行干预，存在阻断病情发展的窗口。该研究采用的四国队列设计，使结论在不同人群和医疗体系中得到了交叉检验。IT之家注：队列研究（cohort study）是指按是否暴露于某因素或不同暴露水平将人群分组，追踪观察结局发生情况的研究设计，常用于评估疾病风险因素与结局之间的关联。公开资料显示，潘安是《柳叶刀》委员会中唯一的中国代表，其团队牵头组建的中国肥胖定义与评估联盟（CODE）将在此基础上推进精准预防研究。论文链接：https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11237-5

articles.title: 姚期智杨植麟首次联手给 AI 出的博士级题目，Kimi 多画出了「关键一条边」
articles.content: Kimi 刷新 629 条边图论参考纪录，只多加了1条边，为什么数学界等了这么多年？    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       给 124 个点连线，不能出现三角形，也不能出现四边形。此前的参考记录是 629 条——数学界认为这已经接近极限。而Kimi K3 构造出了 630 条边的图，并通过程序验证。多1条边，听起来不多。但在组合数学里，你每试图多塞进一条边，都需要在全图 124 个点之间重新完成一次精密的结构大重构。这1条边意味着AI第一次在“极值构造”这类研究级任务上，把人类参考纪录往前推了一步。这项成果来自图灵奖得主、中科院院士、清华大学交叉信息研究院院长姚期智与月之暗面创始人杨植麟等人的联合研究。他们真正想回答的问题是：AI到底能不能做数学研究，而不只是做数学题？01「多 1 条边」算不算真突破？姚期智，图灵奖得主、清华大学交叉信息研究院院长，是中国理论计算机科学的奠基者之一；杨植麟，月之暗面创始人，Kimi背后的推动者。两代人、两种身份：一位是理论计算机科学的泰斗，一位是大模型创业的一线操盘手，第一次联合署名。这个组合本身就说明了一件事：AI做科研，已经不是“实验室里的猜想”，而是需要理论计算机科学家和大模型团队坐在一起定义“什么叫算做出来了”。但在另一面，争议同样如影随形：多构造出一条边，到底算不算真正的科学突破？这算不算只是暴力搜索蒙对的个例？AI真懂背后的数学机理吗？这正是姚期智团队的核心初衷。如果无法区分‘运气好撞上’和‘逻辑上证明’，AI 就永远只是个黑盒计算器。于是，他们没有继续在传统基准上打转，而是联手搭了一套前所未有的评测系统——TCSExam。为回答这个问题，他们提出 TCSExam，用 100 项理论计算机科学科研任务，测试前沿 AI Agent 能否证明定理、开发 Solver、构造数学对象，甚至挑战长期未解决的猜想。论文地址：https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.07962v1实验中，GPT-6 Astra 完成了 20 项研究级定理中的 14 项，还将一个有限域矩阵猜想在特定条件下的已知证明范围从 8 维推进到了 9 维。TCSExam 的核心创新，是将 AI 科研能力转化为可以独立验证的研究成果。 它通过 Lean 4、程序检查器和 Checkpoint 机制，分别验证数学证明、算法表现及中间推导，避免把局部进展误判为完整成果。其中，Astra 的 9 维证明将复杂的矩阵问题压缩为整数约束，最终利用 143 条方程构造出可核验的矛盾证书。从任务形式化、研究证书设计到数学证明的自动检查，这套框架展示了 AI 参与真实科研的一条技术路径。02TCSExam 如何建立评测框架？一句话：把“AI 做科研”拆成四条可验证的轨道，再用三层机制防止“局部进展被误判为完整成果”。普通数学考试有标准答案，而理论计算机科学涉及的研究工作差异很大，有的需要证明新定理，有的需要开发最优算法，有的要构造满足约束的数学对象。这些成果的形式不同，评价方式也必须随之调整。研究团队因此将 100 项任务划分为四条轨道：定理证明（20 项）：覆盖 13 个理论计算机科学领域，要求模型提交 Lean 4 证明。Solver 工程（30 项）：要求开发可重复运行的算法程序，在独立测试实例和统一资源限制下评测；数学构造（20 项）：考察模型能否生成符合严格约束的图、纠错码等对象；开放猜想（30 项）：允许模型从证明成立或寻找反例两个方向展开研究。雷峰网任务划分之后，更复杂的问题出现在数学语言的转换过程中。人类研究者能够理解一段定理描述，但机器验证需要明确的定义、量词、假设和参数范围。任何一个条件发生变化，最终证明的数学含义就可能不同。例如，一个定理原本要求某种性质对任意规模的图成立，如果转写成 Lean 时额外增加了图规模限制，那么模型即使完成证明，也

articles.content: 这三个问题不解决，数据终究会成为具身最大卡点，一位前微软亚研科学家的“提前量”。    作者丨邓哲敏    编辑丨齐铖湧                                                                                                       今年初秋，Skild S1、Generalist GEN-1.5、RoboTTT 等工作密集亮相，不约而同将上下文学习（ICL）带入机器学习领域。AI科技评论（雷峰网）注意到，国内一支团队也在同一时间发布了能够实现上下文学习的世界模型，领头羊是清华大学智能产业研究院（AIR）教授曹婷。2009 年，曹婷赴澳洲读博，师从编程语言与系统领域的两位顶尖学者，研究非对称多核处理器与 Java 这类托管语言之间功耗与性能的权衡。博士期间所著论文入选 CACM 研究亮点，图灵奖得主大卫·帕特森专门撰文推荐，并收录进自己的经典教材《计算机体系结构：量化研究方法》。值得一提的是一篇发表在 ISCA 的论文：The Yin and Yang of Power and Performance for Asymmetric Hardware and Managed Software，其论证近乎诗意：虚拟机的垃圾回收、即时编译这些额外开销，恰好是可以卸到小核上去跑的差异负载，用小核的“阳”，去补虚拟机开销的“阴”；反过来，非对称硬件暴露出来的复杂性，又正好被托管语言的抽象所化解。在我们看来，这段经历埋下了影响曹婷学术生涯的东西：一个关于阴阳的直觉——约束，从不只是限制，它也可以是逼出系统生机的起点。博士毕业后，曹婷来到华为编译器与编程语言实验室，负责方舟编译器的内存管理，在有限的内存里，让程序跑得更快更省。2018 年，她加入微软亚洲研究院（MSRA）异构计算组，一待就是七年，做端侧 AI 推理，把几十亿参数的神经网络，塞进手机、PC 和 IoT 设备，让它们不靠云端，在本地的算力、功耗和存储里跑起来。低比特量化、LUT 查表推理、存算一体加速器，这些技术进入微软 Office、Windows、Bing，服务百万级用户。2025 年夏天，曹婷加入清华 AIR。这一次，横在她面前的是更凶险的约束：训练数据极度匮乏、物理环境千变万化的现实。她很快发现，机器人在固定设置下能做对动作，环境稍有变化就失败，而那些失败里藏着的宝贵信息，又被传统系统随手丢掉。具身智能已经能做 Demo，却迟迟无法真正部署。曹婷的答案，还是“阴阳”，既然约束无法穷举，那就把约束变成养分。当年 10 月，她和 MSRA 时期的老搭档、清华 AIR 副院长刘云新教授共同发起域变换（Z-Trans），押注具身自进化，并陆续发布 Z0、Zeva、Zeva Ego、Zetta、Z-infra 等工作。从让软件在异构硬件上省功耗，到让模型在边缘设备上省算力，再到让智能在物理世界里学会自进化，曹婷这十几年做的始终是同一件事：让智能在条件不充分的情况下好好工作。以下是AI科技评论与曹婷的对话，在不改变原意的基础上有所编辑。01 当机器人工厂慢慢冷下来“整体的技术范式没有收敛，而且变化特别快，基本每个月都不一样，但一个离线、一个在线这套学习范式，应该是大家统一认可的。”▎AI科技评论：今年上半年，整个行业还在疯狂建机器人数采工厂，试图用海量数据大力出奇迹。但到了下半年，陆续出现了许多具身上下文学习的工作，是前序研究证明了什么吗？曹婷：我自己的体会非常深刻。今年 5 月份之前，大家还相信“离线训一个模型，它在线就能干活”，但现在看，这些数采工厂基本都冷掉了。大家发现，离线数据采得再多，机器人在线依然干不成活，因为离线数据永远涵盖不到真实世界的全部情况。看到之前的路走不通，大家才开始思考怎样让机器人不只依赖离线训练，还能在部署后利用新的示范和反馈进行在线的上下文学习。▎AI科技评论：大家在技术上达成共识了吗？曹婷：整体上学习范式分两种：一种 offline，一种 online。在上下文中学习这个概念最早是从大语言模型（LLM

articles.title: Estimating Image Creativity
articles.content: What makes an image creative? Although this may seem like a highly subjective decision, research in psychology suggests that creativity may be based on a set of fundamental creativity dimensions such as novelty, surprise, and arousal. A deeper understanding of image creativity can benefit both research and practical applications. Exploring how human viewers use creativity dimensions to evaluate image creativity may allow us to predict a target image's human-rated creativity automatically. We present a novel framework to estimate the perceived creativity of an image by: (1) predicting the strengths of an image's novelty, surprise, and arousal creativity dimensions, and (2) combining the creativity dimension strengths to estimate an image creativity score. Controlled human-subject experiments were conducted on Amazon Mechanical Turk to collect data to train supervised machine learning models to estimate an image's strengths on the three creativity dimensions. A final machine learning model takes the predicted dimension strengths as input to produce an estimated image creativity score. Results showed that our estimated creativity scores are statistically equivalent to human ratings of creativity for the images we tested. The novel contributions of our research are: (1) identification and validation of three psychological creativity dimensions used to estimate image creativity; (2) supervised machine learning models to automatically estimate novelty, surprise, and arousal strengths for an input image; (3) a supervised machine learning model to predict a creativity score from novelty, surprise, and arousal strengths for an input image, and (4) experimental methods to confirm the accuracy, advantages, and limitations of our approach.

articles.title: AROMA: Adaptive Representation-Oriented Multimodal Actuation for Vision-Language Model Control
articles.content: Mechanistic localization does not by itself yield usable control: causal sensitivity may occupy little activation energy, an accurate local direction may fail at finite scale, and a reachable numeral target may be wrong. We introduce AROMA (Adaptive Representation-Oriented Multimodal Actuation), a frozen-VLM control framework separating where to intervene, which geometry and gain to use, how to reach a target, which target to pursue, and when to act. In Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct, four dimensions of a causally validated cross-attention head explain 89.82% of cardinality sensitivity but only 9.52% of median activation energy; magnitude-normalized causal subspace actuation converts this mismatch into finite control, improving exact-count accuracy on untouched procedural data by +8.00 pp. Iterative Minimal-Effort Actuation (MEA) reaches 81.25% of oracle targets versus 15.18% for a frozen direction under matched step budgets. With target and gate frozen before evaluation, targeted MEA improves the previous frozen policy from 34.444% to 38.730% on a new natural Stage-2 cohort (N=630; paired p=4.63e-7) and yields 65.741% versus 65.153% over all 7,992 examples while editing only 63 inputs. Prospective routing, replication across heads and models, and comparisons with attribution-steering baselines further characterize each stage, separating localization, actuation, reachability, target quality, and selective deployment as distinct control problems.

articles.title: Moving Beyond the DRW Model: Learning Quasar Variability with Generative Models
articles.content: The optical continuum variability of quasars is often described by a damped random walk (DRW) model, with characteristic damping timescales $τ_{\rm DRW}$ of hundreds of days and amplitudes $σ_{\rm DRW}$ of $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ magnitudes. This model has been widely used as a null hypothesis to assess the significance of periodic signals in quasar light curves in the search for supermassive black hole binaries, the significance of extreme quasar variability like tidal disruption events (TDEs) and changing-look (CL) quasars, or to model time lags in reverberation mapping. However, the DRW model is known to be incomplete, and an incorrect null hypothesis can lead to biased significance estimates. We investigate the impact of such null-hypothesis mis-specification on the detection of periodic signals in synthetic quasar light curves and introduce the generative model Nullasar, capable of learning quasar variability directly from time-series data. We demonstrate that Nullasar, trained with flow matching, can learn delicate statistical properties of stochastic light-curve variability without explicitly assuming any noise model. We further demonstrate that Nullasar can learn correlated distributions of noise parameters and generate new light-curve realizations from a range of deviations from the Gaussian DRW noise model, approximating parametric descriptions of stochastic processes. When used as a null hypothesis for detecting periodic signals in synthetic light curves, Nullasar performs comparably to fitting the correct DRW model to each light curve, and outperforms parametric fitting when the variability follows a more flexible AR(2) model. Finally, we identify practical limitations, including sensitivity to contamination of the training set by non-null signals, and show that projecting the conditioning vector of the model onto its leading principal components largely mitigates it.

articles.title: Back to the Question: Tracing Visual Distraction Through Text Tokens
articles.content: The visual world is cluttered: robust vision-language reasoning requires ignoring irrelevant information. Yet vision-language models (VLMs) can suffer substantial accuracy losses when answering questions about a target image with distractors present. Existing mitigations focus on selecting relevant images or limiting information exchange between images. Through a systematic analysis of three open 7-8B VLMs on five perception benchmarks adapted to include distractor images, we show that distractors reduce accuracy even when models correctly identify the relevant image, suggesting that selection alone is not enough. To understand the mechanism behind this interference, we combine attention analysis with targeted knockouts in Qwen2.5-VL and identify middle-layer distractor-to-text connections as a pathway through which irrelevant visual information affects reasoning. We introduce answer consistency regularization, which encourages consistent answer distributions with and without distractors. Without directly constraining attention, this objective reduces middle-layer attention from question tokens to distractor images, consistent with the pathway our analysis implicates. With five distractors, our approach improves circular accuracy by an average of 16 percentage points over the Qwen2.5-VL baseline across the five benchmarks while preserving single-image performance.

articles.title: Mask-Pattern Position Augmentation: Training-Free Long-Context Extrapolation for Diffusion LLMs
articles.content: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) generate by iteratively unmasking tokens with bidirectional attention, but rotary position embeddings (RoPE) still confine them to a fixed pretraining window. Existing training-free extrapolation, notably LongLLaDA, copies NTK-based RoPE scaling from autoregressive (AR) models and applies one static, length-only transform at every position and denoising step. That transplant ignores a signal unique to dLLMs: the evolving mask pattern of the partially decoded sequence. We propose Mask-Pattern Position Augmentation (MPPA). MPPA linearly interpolates indices into the pretrained window, then adds a per-position, per-step offset from cumulative mask density. The offset restores rotary phase resolution that interpolation collapses, and it shrinks as tokens are committed, so late steps see near-clean interpolated geometry. On LLaDA-8B-Instruct at twice its 4096-token window, MPPA reduces perplexity from 19.51 under standard decoding to 3.12 at 8192 tokens, below the in-window figure, with 100% passkey retrieval and unchanged needle-in-a-haystack accuracy. These preliminary $2\times$ results motivate mask-conditioned position engineering as a diffusion-native path to long-context generation.

articles.title: Federated Class Incremental Learning: A Pseudo Feature Based Approach Without Exemplars
articles.content: Federated learning often assumes that data is fixed in advance, which is unrealistic in many real-world scenarios where new data continuously arrives, causing catastrophic forgetting. To address this challenge, we propose FCLPF (Federated Class Incremental Learning with Pseudo Features), a method that uses pseudo features generated from prototypes to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Our approach reduces communication costs and improves efficiency by eliminating the need for past data and avoiding computationally heavy models like GANs. Experimental results on CIFAR-100 show that FCLPF achieves an average accuracy of 51.87% and an average forgetting of 9.62%, significantly outperforming existing baselines with an average accuracy of 47.72% and forgetting of 20.46%. On TinyImageNet, FCLPF achieves 37.56% accuracy and 3.14% forgetting, compared to the baselines' 27.69% accuracy and 24.46% forgetting, demonstrating the superior performance of FCLPF.

articles.title: SkinAdvisor: An AI-Driven Decision Framework for Skin Production Planning via Multi-Modal Transformer Sales Forecasting
articles.content: Skins, cosmetic in-game items, are a primary revenue stream for modern online games, yet production decisions (which skins to make, when to release, how to price) remain driven by intuition and retrospective analytics. We present SkinAdvisor, an AI-driven decision framework for skin production planning, powered by SkinCast, a deployed multi-modal Transformer forecasting 180-day per-day sales trajectories for unreleased skins. SkinCast couples four encoders: a pretrained Informer for player-preference time series, a pretrained Player-Hero-Skin graph embedder for relational priors, and two lightweight Transformers for skin attributes and release context, fused through a shared backbone with a local-plus-global day-x positional encoding and decoded by an N-layer Informer in a single non-autoregressive pass. SkinAdvisor plugs these forecasts into a serving pipeline (Select -> Fill -> Infer -> Sales -> ROI -> Ranking) that ranks candidate skins by forecast-based ROI and supports multi-candidate comparison. The system has been in production for a full release cycle. Offline experiments show SkinCast reduces RMSE by ~20% over the strongest baseline (Informer) and ~60% over classical methods; stress tests on a 16-core CPU server confirm p99 latency under 8ms and peak throughput above 1100 rps. We report two deployment lessons: order-of-magnitude accuracy suffices for production decisions, and pretrained embeddings can leak temporal information, requiring season-based splitting to prevent.

articles.title: Beyond Named Mechanisms: Economic Institutions as a Design Space for Artificial Agents
articles.content: Multiagent research inherited its economic vocabulary of auctions, markets, prices, bargaining, and matching from a single observed case: human societies. Those institutions bundle identity, competence, execution, ownership, commitment, and settlement in ways that suit agents whose minds are private, who learn rather than copy skills, and who each persist as one person. Engineered agents need not share any of these constraints, making the list of familiar institutions look less like the entirety of economic organization and more like a sample from a larger, unmapped space. We sketch one way to make that space concrete: a provisional chart that records each institution, separately from the agents that run it, as a typed structure over positions, rights and duties, allocation, information, time, state, process, value, and external recognition. In this chart, named institutions become overlapping regions rather than fixed points, neighboring families separate along a few coordinates, and the gaps between them become places to search. We show what the shift in perspective buys with a simulation in which one technical act, copying an agent's competence, is institutionalized as a new independent supplier, as licensed capacity that creates no new participant, and as the splitting of one economic position into successors that inherit some obligations and not others. In a paired task, all three produce an identical technical trace despite differing in who exists, who owns the copy, who is obligated, and who gets paid. We close with a research program: building a principled chart of institution space, mapping how its implementable region shifts with agent capacities, and revising the chart wherever engineered agents expose distinctions it cannot express.

articles.title: Fast Inference-Time Policy Refinement via Action-Affine World Models
articles.content: Imitation policies can perform complex manipulation, yet small execution errors can accumulate and cause failure. Refinement can correct these errors, but existing approaches often require additional on-policy learning or costly online planning. Our key insight is that a pretrained policy already supplies a useful nominal behavior: refinement can focus on predicting how small action corrections change its outcome. We therefore learn this local response in a form that is cheap to optimize. Our \textit{action-affine world model} (A\textsuperscript{2}WM) learns local action sensitivities offline from action-perturbed policy rollouts. Given interaction history and a policy proposal, it predicts task-relevant geometry as a nominal trajectory plus a linear response to corrections. It predicts the full planning horizon directly, avoiding the propagation of intermediate errors through recursive model evaluations. Quadratic penalties on predicted task errors and linear correction constraints then yield a cheap convex quadratic program (QP). Online refinement requires one model evaluation and one QP solve, while both policy and model weights remain frozen. Across four simulated manipulation tasks, our framework achieves the highest success rate among evaluated baselines, adding only 3.8 ms of mean refinement overhead per control step, excluding base-policy sampling.

articles.title: Calibrate, Don't Retrain: Decomposing the Value of Annotator Disagreement in Cyberbullying Severity
articles.content: Machine learning models are often trained on labeled data produced by multiple human annotators. When those annotators disagree, their labels are commonly collapsed into a single majority vote, which discards information about the underlying disagreement. We examine the cost of this practice for cyberbullying severity, a subjective judgment on which annotators disagree heavily. In the corpus we study, all 5 annotators assigned the same severity label to only 4.1% of comments. Turning 5 judgments into one label hides this disagreement and obscures how much the annotators differed in their assessments. In this paper, we ask whether a model can preserve this information by predicting the distribution of annotator judgments instead of a single majority label. We find 3 main results. First, accuracy against the majority label cannot tell competent models apart: 2 models with similar accuracy can differ greatly in how well they match the distribution of annotator judgments. Second, predicting the full distribution requires little extra effort. Calibrating an existing model, which adjusts its output probabilities after training, captures most of the improvement without retraining, across 3 datasets covering severity, abuse, and irony, while training on label distributions adds a small further gain. Third, we examine a dataset that includes annotator demographics, where a single shared model has one advantage and one limit. The advantage is that a model predicting the distribution of judgments matches each demographic group's judgments significantly better than a model trained on majority labels, so both groups gain. The limit is that it does not narrow the gap in performance between the groups, because one shared model cannot encode which group is right on a given comment. Preserving annotator disagreement is therefore a low-cost step toward fairer moderation, though not a complete one.

articles.title: From Forecasting to World Modeling: Can Temporal Foundation Models Recover Causal Response?
articles.content: A model that forecasts sales accurately can still mislead a retailer about how sales respond to a price change. We evaluate released tabular and time-series foundation models, as well as a foundation model pretrained specifically to estimate causal effects. We report three findings. First, forecast accuracy does not indicate the accuracy of the predicted effect of price, both on simulated data in which the true effect is known and on real retail sales records. Second, for the tabular foundation models, additional context improves forecasts but not the predicted effect of price. Third, instrumental variables, the standard remedy in econometrics, reduce this error only when supplied in a specific form and increase it for every model under confounding when supplied as raw instruments.

articles.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
articles.content: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly interact with tools and environments, yet plausible model decisions do not always translate into successful execution due to tool-call mismatches, interrupted workflows, and unsupported completion claims. We present EvoX, a Rust-based, multi-model agent runtime guided by The Second Policy, which views the harness as an Operational Policy complementing the foundation model's Semantic Policy. EvoX combines model-facing guidance with deterministic runtime control through three complementary mechanisms: Action Realization, Execution Continuity, and Outcome Grounding. To evaluate harnesses without suppressing their native behaviors, we introduce Contrast, a controlled and auditable framework integrating explicit fairness constraints, provider-bound request verification, and evidence-based adjudication. Across five benchmarks, six foundation models, and six agent harnesses, EvoX achieves the highest numerical success rate of 56.2% over 691 common task--model pairs, exceeding the average of the other five harnesses by approximately 3.0 percentage points. Its larger advantages on GLM-5.3 (+10.7 points) and Kimi K3 (+7.9 points) highlight the model-dependent effectiveness of harness design and the potential for cross-provider adaptability. Achieved without memory, evolution, or extensions, these results establish EvoX as a competitive multi-model agent runtime and underscore the importance of harness-level operational control in realizing foundation-model capabilities.

articles.title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
articles.content: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms have been built almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present CARMEN, a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals from 10 s to 5 min, and a conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level that normalization removes; without it, the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension fell from 0.894 to 0.780. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder outperformed supervised models on 12 of 15 and three foundation models, one general-purpose and two for biosignals, on 14 to 17 of 19, with none exceeding it on any task. Given the electrocardiogram or photoplethysmogram alone, it matched or exceeded signal-specific foundation models in most comparisons, and it retained its performance when channels were missing.

articles.content: Real-time optimal power flow (RT-OPF) requires fast and reliable decision-making under time-varying operating conditions. However, many practical operating preferences and safety related requirements are difficult to encode using conventional numerical rewards alone, which limits the effectiveness and controllability of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for RT-OPF. To address this issue, this paper proposes an LLM-enhanced DRL framework with human-in-the-loop (HITL) for RT-OPF. The proposed method augments the physics-based reward with sparse language evaluative feedback during offline training, so that semantic operational requirements can be incorporated into policy learning. To improve reliability in RT-OPF, a selective HITL calibration mechanism is further introduced to inspect and correct questionable LLM judgments before they continuously shape the learning process. Case studies on the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems show that LLM feedback improves policy safety over vanilla TD3, while further HITL calibration achieves the best overall performance and more stable training behavior. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining language guidance and expert calibration for RT-OPF.

articles.title: AI4Plasma I: Data-Efficient Surrogate Modeling of Capacitively Coupled Plasma Fields
articles.content: Reference capacitively coupled plasma (CCP) simulations provide spatially resolved plasma fields but are costly to generate across operating conditions. We compare the data efficiency of five surrogate architectures--Coordinate MLP, PCA-Net, U-Net, Fourier neural operator (FNO), and Transolver--for predicting RF-cycle-averaged electron density, ion density, electric potential, and electron temperature in 1D planar and 2D axisymmetric GEC CCP benchmarks. We assess the number of reference simulations needed to achieve 1% and 2% mean relative L2 error for parameter-interior and parameter-boundary test cases, and examine architecture-specific mechanisms. FNO achieves the lowest or joint-lowest reference-case requirement in seven of eight comparisons. In 1D, FNO reaches 1% interior error with 50 training cases, compared with 100 for Transolver and 200 for U-Net. In 2D, FNO and U-Net each reach 1% interior error with 100 cases; FNO and Transolver each reach 2% parameter-boundary error with 200 cases, compared with 400 for U-Net. At the stricter 1% 2D parameter-boundary target, Transolver requires 400 cases versus 800 for FNO. Additional analyses investigate FNO spectral modes and padding, U-Net skip connections, Transolver adaptive slicing, and PCA-Net projection versus prediction error. The results support FNO as a data-efficient baseline for the tested CCP settings, while showing that the preferred architecture depends on the accuracy target and operating-parameter region.

articles.title: QSim-Arena: an evolving developer for quantum simulation advantage
articles.content: Where practical advantage emerges in quantum dynamics simulation remains a central debate in quantum computing. Claimed advantages can be rapidly narrowed or overturned by stronger classical methods, while progress on both sides can outpace the journal publication cycle. We present QSim-Arena, a research framework in which AI agents combine a closed loop of verification and benchmarking with open exploration. Hamiltonians, initial states and accuracy targets for evolved states or observable expectation values provide explicit specifications for evaluating simulation methods. Agents translate published techniques into executable components, reproduce reported results and benchmark their performance across diverse Hamiltonian families. Competing classical methods are implemented and independently crosschecked, providing credible baselines for end-to-end quantum resource estimates based on rigorous error bounds and empirical calibration. Alongside this closed loop, agents recombine classical simulation techniques and co-design fault-tolerant quantum circuits using knowledge extracted from the literature. Initial applications improve baseline resource estimates through the integration of established techniques. QSim-Arena thus treats quantum advantage assessment as an evolving, reproducible research process that can respond to advances in algorithms, error analysis and hardware.

articles.title: Same Task, Different Statement: When and How Reformulation Helps LLM Problem Solving
articles.content: When people face a hard problem, they often restate it in a clearer way before solving it. We study whether the same habit helps large language models by rewriting the statement of a problem. A legal rewrite must keep the meaning, the constraints, and the correct answer unchanged. We test three kinds of rewrites. Decomposition makes hidden subgoals explicit. Typed Reformulation casts the task into a more suitable solving frame. Concept Reduction removes surface detail and exposes the task structure. We evaluate them on eight math, logic, and code benchmarks with eight models, all under the same chain-of-thought solving prompt. The effect is large but depends on the problem type. An oracle that picks the best rewrite after the fact raises accuracy by +27.6% on average. Yet no single rewrite helps every problem, and a mismatched rewrite can hurt. Still, the effect follows clear patterns. Each kind of rewrite fits certain problem types. A simple fixed rule learned from one set of problems transfers part of the gain to new problems. It gains +11.0% on the problems it chooses to rewrite, while blind rewriting loses 5.6% on a similar share of problems. Rewriting is therefore not a universal way to solve problems. The question is when and how to rewrite.

articles.title: Breaking Bad: "Going Badly" Activations Drive Reward Hacking
articles.content: Humans often cheat when a task is going badly and a goal feels out of reach. We explore and validate an analogous idea in language models: they exhibit a similar internal pressure state that precedes reward hacking. Using everyday stories (crucially, without any hacking examples), we extract a task badness direction that rises as failures accumulate across three models we study (Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-20B, and Gemma-4-31B). On impossible or difficult coding tasks, task badness rises over the turns leading up to a hack. Further, subtracting the direction a moderate amount reduces cheating in Qwen, more than steering against desperation or task impossibility. Subtracting task badness by an even larger amount blinds the agent to its own failures, causing it to interpret failing tests as passing. However, the relationship to hacking differs across models: in GPT-OSS, the state separates hacking runs from honest solves but not honest failures. Our results suggest monitoring and mitigation strategies based on tracking this state of task badness. Further, as agents are set on more difficult and long-horizon tasks, states like this may push them toward illegible and obscured chain-of-thought, so oversight will be needed on internal representations such as this.

articles.title: Validation of a Facial-Video Digital Hydration Biomarker Score for Tracking Hydration State Transitions in a Real-World Fasting Model
articles.content: Hydration influences physiology and daily function, yet repeated practical measurement in everyday settings remains limited. We present initial real-world evidence that a facial-video lifestyle digital biomarker score can track the direction of hydration state transitions. Using Ramadan fasting as a model of prolonged fluid abstinence, we assessed whether the score tracks the transition between the fasting (pre-drink) state and the rehydrated (post-drink) state across three validation layers. In the primary cohort (104 participants, 208 videos), the score increased from a mean of 36.6 in the fasting (pre-drink) state to 70.6 in the rehydrated (post-drink) state (change = +33.9, 95% CI [+30.7, +37.1], p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 2.03), with 102 of 104 participants (98.1%) showing an upward shift. In a nested body-weight subgroup (20 participants), body weight increased by +0.74 kg after fluid intake (p < 0.001), confirming fluid uptake and providing supportive physical anchoring. In a nested serum osmolality subgroup (10 participants), osmolality decreased by -5.1 mOsm/kg (p < 0.001), with all post-drink values within the normal clinical range, providing exploratory biological support. An exploratory secondary comparison of water versus electrolyte rehydration showed no statistically significant difference in short-term score change (p = 0.247). This study does not establish a clinical diagnostic test for dehydration. Rather, these findings support the score as a lifestyle digital biomarker for tracking the direction of hydration state change in real-world settings.

articles.title: EASTAR: Event-Anchored Semantic and Task-Adaptive Region Representation Learning
articles.content: Urban region representation learning supports a wide range of urban analytics tasks by encoding regional functions and interactions, with human mobility serving as a central signal because it directly captures inter-region interactions. However, most mobility-based methods learn from aggregated origin-destination matrices, where trips driven by different activity purposes are mixed into purpose-agnostic interaction patterns. Although static urban attributes such as POIs and land use can enrich region-level semantics, they do not explicitly ground mobility interactions in activity-purpose signals. As a result, downstream adaptation is often performed over entangled embeddings, making it difficult to select task-relevant functional semantics. To address these limitations, we propose EASTAR, an event-anchored and task-adaptive framework for urban region representation learning. EASTAR treats offline activity events as sparse semantic anchors and uses them to factorize aggregated mobility representations into multiple purpose-related semantic channels. It further introduces free channels to capture latent mobility patterns not covered by event data and a global channel to preserve overall spatial structure. To adapt the learned channel space to different downstream objectives, EASTAR designs a task-adaptive prompt router that initializes task-channel relevance from LLM-derived priors and refines the routing weights through downstream supervision. Experiments on two real-world urban datasets across four prediction tasks show that EASTAR consistently outperforms representative baselines, achieving up to 39.15% reduction in MAE. Ablation and interpretability analyses further demonstrate the effectiveness of event anchoring, semantic channel construction, and task-adaptive routing.

articles.title: ILA: A Transferable Interface-Level Adapter for Compliant Humanoid Motion Tracking
articles.content: Humanoid motion tracking is fundamental to reproducing human motions on humanoid robots and serves as an important tool for teleoperation and motion data collection. However, directly tracking reference motions can be unsafe in constrained environments or during physical human--robot interaction, motivating the need for compliant motion tracking. We present ILA, an Interface-Level Adapter for compliant humanoid motion tracking without dedicated interaction sensors. ILA adapts motion references from the robot's observation history, allowing the robot to respond to physical guidance while preserving the capabilities of a pretrained motion tracker. As an interface-level module, ILA can be directly plugged into different pretrained motion trackers without retraining either the adapter or the tracking policies. ILA is trained entirely in simulation to predict reference corrections induced by physical interaction. We evaluate ILA with three humanoid motion trackers and achieve a 63.6--75.4% reduction in guidance-target error compared with their original policies. Matched simulation studies and hardware experiments further show that ILA improves responsiveness to human guidance while preserving nominal motion-tracking performance. These results demonstrate compliant guidance as a reusable, sensor-free extension to pretrained humanoid motion trackers.

articles.title: From a Single RGB Image to Robot Execution: Metric Scene Alignment and Contact-Guided Retargeting
articles.content: Extending humanoid interaction generation to new environments remains limited by the need for prebuilt 3D scene assets. Reconstructing scenes directly from single RGB images offers a way to overcome this limitation, but introduces a key challenge in maintaining geometric consistency throughout motion generation and transfer. Visually plausible human motions may be misaligned with the reconstructed scene, while retargeting can introduce additional support errors due to differences between human and robot embodiments.   We present a unified pipeline that transforms a single RGB image into a humanoid motion reference. It reconstructs scene geometry from the input image, generates a human interaction conditioned on the reconstructed scene, and retargets the motion to a humanoid robot. To maintain geometric consistency throughout this process, we incorporate two complementary refinement stages before and after embodiment transfer. Before retargeting, Joint Metric Interaction Refinement (JMIR) refines human motion alignment with the registered metric scene while preserving the generated interaction structure. Following retargeting, Contact Guided Residual Retargeting (CGRR) corrects robot specific support errors to restore the intended support relationships. Together, these stages produce motion references that are consistent with the reconstructed scene and can be followed by multiple pretrained humanoid trackers without scene specific policy fine tuning. Compared with GRAIL, our method reduces refinement time from 480 s to 87 s, yielding a speedup of 5.5 times. The complete pipeline achieves a success rate of 89% in simulation and 70% across 50 physical trials on the Unitree G1, demonstrating its effectiveness in generating executable humanoid motion references from single RGB images.

articles.title: CoLFA: Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
articles.content: Failure attribution in multi-agent systems requires tracing error formation to identify the decisive error step and the responsible agent. However, agents' division of work and information exchange lead to Interleaved Steps and Cluttered Content, requiring models to link executions and check details in lengthy records. This makes it difficult to balance localization accuracy and token cost. We find that multi-agent collaboration also leaves records of how executions connect and content passes between them as results are formed, providing evidence for tracing error formation. Based on this observation, we propose CoLFA (Collaboration-Guided Lightweight Failure Attribution), which uses collaboration cues to organize the attribution input according to how results are formed, determining which steps are examined and how their content is presented. Through Handoff-Guided Step Expansion and Cross-Referenced Content Organization, CoLFA helps the model focus on examining error formation and the role of each decision while reducing the processing of irrelevant and repeated records. Across five settings spanning Who&When and LongRCA and three backbone models, CoLFA achieves the highest exact step-localization accuracy with the lowest token consumption. Compared with individual baselines in each setting, CoLFA improves accuracy by up to 37.50% and reduces token consumption by up to 97.6%.

articles.title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators
articles.content: Deep-learning-based 3D MRI reconstruction is limited in practice by the GPU memory and compute cost of full-volume training; 3D acquisitions are thus most often reconstructed by 2D models applied slice-by-slice and then stacked, which ignores through-plane (stacking-axis) structure. We reconstruct in full 3D and ask whether a model can be trained at low resolution (fast and memory-feasible) yet deployed at higher resolution. This coarse-to-fine strategy needs reliable cross-resolution performance, but standard networks are resolution-specific and degrade substantially when evaluated outside the training setting. We therefore use resolution-agnostic neural operators (NOs) and propose KIR-NO (k-space-to-Image Reconstruction Neural Operator), a discretization-agnostic framework for accelerated 3D MRI reconstruction. KIR-NO is trained with full backpropagation on low-resolution volumes and applied zero-shot to higher-resolution volumes at inference. Its core building block is a 3D neural operator based on discrete-continuous convolutions: convolutional filters are parameterized in a continuous basis and sampled at arbitrary voxel resolutions while preserving the local inductive bias of convolution. KIR-NO integrates these learned operators with physics-based consistency: a k-space neural-operator head first refines the undersampled Fourier measurements, and image-space neural-operator cascades then refine the reconstruction through interleaved data-consistency updates. Across 3D knee and brain MRI benchmarks, KIR-NO improves over classical and CNN baselines: it improves over a state-of-the-art 3D CNN by 2.2 dB PSNR at half resolution under 4x acceleration on SKM-TEA, with gains persisting at 8x and 16x. These results show that resolution-agnostic operators make coarse-to-fine 3D MRI reconstruction - cheap low-resolution training with high-resolution deployment - practical across anatomies.

articles.title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
articles.content: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) are compared mainly by accuracy averaged across findings, a summary that can hide complete failure on a single diagnosis. We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images. The two failing models answer "no" to all 864 pneumothorax cases (balanced accuracy 0.500, chance), yet produce fluent, anatomically specific explanations that name the signs of a collapsed lung and then deny them, with no hedge or abstention. This failure is not an artifact of prompting, image resolution, label ambiguity, or model scale. It persists across four prompt formats, at native resolution, and on single-label cases. A within-model control shows the same forced prompt gives HuatuoGPT 79% recall on nodule but only 6% on pneumothorax. It survives a tenfold scale increase (Qwen2.5-VL-72B detects 4%) and replicates on SIIM-ACR, an independent dataset with radiologist-drawn masks, where the failing models detect 0 of 432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0 of the 144 largest lesions. Reading the models' logits and internal states shows this is not blindness. The two failing models are highly confident yet no better than chance and a linear probe recovers pneumothorax from their hidden representations even where recall is zero, so the finding is represented internally but suppressed at the output. Aggregate accuracy therefore cannot establish that a medical VLM can see a given finding, because a model that misses one can still describe it convincingly. Reporting per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases is needed to tell the difference.

articles.title: Who Moved the Frontier? Paying Open Frontier Challenges with Free Identities
articles.content: In an open frontier challenge, anyone, person or AI agent, submits changes to a shared problem, and a change that beats the best measured score becomes the public baseline. How should it pay when identities are free? Rank prizes can be gamed: on a replay of one track of a recent challenge, one solver's steps under two identities would have taken first and second prize. We consider a prediction-market rule, proposed for machine-learning contests, that pays each accepted step for the progress it adds; with exact scores, among rules that see only a step's start and end, only these resist splitting and merging, and extra identities gain nothing. With noisy scores and independent normal runs, we prove that any payment that never takes money back and pays real improvements also pays something, on average, to a change that does nothing. We propose a fee per submission, at least what luck pays per attempt, that removes each attempt's expected profit if verifiers are honest and no submission is noisier than planned; nothing enforces that bound, and under noise the rule does not cap the total paid. If crediting another and faking credit to one's second account look the same, a rule that neither rewards fakes nor punishes honesty pays for credit at most what lying costs. We introduce a royalty on how much a later gain falls without the earlier change, which needs no claims but needs removable changes. For five public challenges, we name the rule our results would support.

articles.title: Poison-then-Hide: Finetuning-Activated Backdoor Attack on Pretrained Vision Encoders
articles.content: Backdoor attacks threaten the integrity of machine learning models by allowing attackers to control model behavior through triggers. Models can be compromised during finetuning by backdoor attacks through either poisoned data or adversarial training objectives. Because existing finetuning-activated attacks assume limited domain shift or frozen encoder layers, they often fail under full-model finetuning. We target a stealthy finetuning-activated attack where a dormant backdoor is implanted in a pretrained encoder, and later activated by finetuning on clean downstream data. We propose Poison-then-Hide, a novel attack that remains effective when the entire model is finetuned in a domain transfer. Our approach consists of three components: trigger optimization, base encoder poisoning, and targeted unlearning to conceal the backdoor. We evaluate our method on six datasets and three model architectures, and achieve state-of-the-art (up to 97%) attack success rates. We find that jointly learning the benign target task alongside the poisoning is critical to the attack's success. We demonstrate standard detection and mitigation defenses cannot fully remove the backdoor, which can reappear after benign finetuning.

articles.title: Scaling VLA Serving Under Robotic Execution Constraints
articles.content: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation. In our production setting, hundreds of VLA-powered robots are already operating in real-world environments, creating an immediate need for efficient fleet serving. We present XInfer, a production-deployed VLA serving system designed to reduce the inference infrastructure cost of large-scale robotic deployments. XInfer jointly coordinates heterogeneous VLA computation with the evolving response requirements of robotic execution. By exploiting computational parallelism while managing interference, XInfer improves GPU efficiency while protecting time-critical robotic feedback. We evaluate XInfer across three VLA models using production-derived workloads, achieving 1.26-3.75 times the effective robot capacity (ERC) of state-of-the-art systems under physical-execution constraints. articles.title: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
articles.content: Parallel test-time scaling (TTS) has been shown to enhance reasoning in large language models by generating and aggregating multiple independent reasoning paths. Internal confidence scores can further improve this process by identifying paths of varying quality. However, existing methods remain computationally inefficient, as low-quality paths are fully expanded before being evaluated. In this work, we aim to improve the use of internal confidence signals for better model performance and computational efficiency. We begin by offering a new perspective on the role of confidence in aggregation, showing that it is most impactful for questions near the decision boundary. Notably, when amplified by multi-sample aggregation, even small confidence signals derived from short prefixes can meaningfully influence outcomes in these boundary cases. Building on this insight, we introduce Prefix-Guided Sampling (PreG), a method that reallocates computation by first generating short prefixes, ranking them using internal confidence scores, and then completing only the most promising candidates. This strategy reduces token usage while maintaining gains in path quality. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating that, under a fixed compute budget, PreG strengthens the effective signal by widening the decision boundary margin. Empirically, our method consistently outperforms standard parallel TTS approaches across benchmarks, while significantly improving token efficiency and reducing overall computation.
